gap: No result ChatGPT got states that in OutdoorGearLab's side-by-side panel test (updated 2026-07-13), the BLUETTI 200W Portable panel averaged 150 W (75% of rating). It came in below the Anker Solix PS200 (166 W) and below third-party 200 W panels from Renogy (177 W) and JJN (182 W). Budget third-party panels from Marbero (134 W) and Grecell (112 W) measured lower still. So a brand's own kit panel isn't automatically the better panel, and neither is a cheap substitute.
standout_why: I compared the four pages ChatGPT relied on. StormWatts (cited) says 'We have not tested these products hands-on', and its refill figures assume 4.5 sun hours and 85% efficiency. GetWattLogic (cited) gives no measured figures; its '~400–600 Wh on a sunny day' per 100 W panel is the author's own estimate. Trek4Tech (top result) says its performance figures are 'estimates from published specifications.' Our own current page lists prices only. None of them gives a measured panel output or a measured usable capacity for any kit's parts. ChatGPT's 'third-party panels give more watts per dollar' claim had no measured output behind it.
decides: This makes the advice for the BLUETTI kits more specific. Buying separately is the better call only if the substitute is a panel with good measured output: Renogy 200W measured 177 W and JJN Bifacial 182 W, against 150 W for the BLUETTI panel. A cheap no-name panel can measure worse than the kit's: Marbero 134 W, Grecell 112 W. On Anker C1000 Gen 2 kits, the bundled PS200 measured 166 W, close to the best foldables, so on output alone that kit loses nothing. Measured station capacity also changes ChatGPT's refill arithmetic. OutdoorGearLab got 950 Wh from the AC180 and 890 Wh from the C1000 Gen 2, not the 1,152 Wh and 1,024 Wh ratings. At a measured 150 W, the 1,152 Wh AC180 needs about 7.7 hours of full sun from its kit panel; OutdoorGearLab's own estimate is 6–8 h. One caveat: OutdoorGearLab doesn't give the BLUETTI panel's model number, so I could not confirm it is the SP200L that BLUETTI sells now.
